problemsEncountered.problem: Work scheduling had been mixed into the personal calendar.
problemsEncountered.effect: Personal and work information were combined, creating clutter.
problemsEncountered.resolution: Philip was removed from the personal calendar and placed on the work calendar.

problemsEncountered.problem: Supervisor calendar editing permissions are not yet confirmed.
problemsEncountered.effect: The supervisor's ability to edit events directly remains uncertain.
problemsEncountered.resolution: Test access during the supervisor meeting and determine whether Google sign-in or additional permission is required.

problemsEncountered.problem: Morning roster notifications are still delivered to the personal account.
problemsEncountered.effect: Notification ownership does not yet match the intended supervisor workflow.
problemsEncountered.resolution: Decide who should receive roster notifications and transfer ownership or delivery later.

problemsEncountered.problem: The supervisor access level has not been selected.

turningPoints.title: Separate tools became one system
turningPoints.description: The calendar, roster, issue form, website, navigation images, and QR resources were connected through one interface.
turningPoints.effectOnDirection: The project moved from assembling individual Google tools to reviewing and governing a functioning communication system.

keyDecisions.decision: Separate work scheduling from the personal calendar.
keyDecisions.reason: Reduce clutter and keep work events in the appropriate calendar.
consequences: Work events are easier to manage.
The personal calendar no longer carries the housekeeping schedule.

keyDecisions.decision: Use one website as the central access point.
keyDecisions.reason: Allow the supervisor to reach schedules, rosters, forms, and resources without searching through separate files.
consequences: The system is easier to navigate.
Mobile and computer access follow the same structure.

keyDecisions.decision: Preserve QR images and reusable materials on a dedicated page.
keyDecisions.reason: Allow the supervisor to retrieve, print, and reuse visual resources.
consequences: QR resources remain available after creation.
The page can later support posters and printable cards.

narrative.methodEstablished: Use a central, mobile-accessible website to connect scheduling, roster visibility, issue reporting, and reusable access materials.
narrative.result: A substantial foundation is complete: the system operates as a connected housekeeping communication website and is ready for supervisor review.
lessonsLearned: Separating personal and work calendars clarifies scheduling.
Embedding operational tools reduces the need to search across separate files.
Visual shortcuts and QR codes make the system easier to enter and reuse.
Permissions and notification ownership must be decided explicitly, even after the interface is functional.
narrative.directionChange: The project advanced from a collection of separate Google tools to a connected communication system requiring governance and access decisions.
narrative.narrativeSummary: The work established the Meadows Housekeeping website as a central interface for calendar, roster, issue reporting, navigation, and QR resources. The remaining work is supervisor review of permissions, notifications, form details, and QR placement.

general.summary: The work update reports that the Meadows Housekeeping website now connects the work calendar, daily roster information, issue form, visual navigation, and QR resources.
keyPoints: Work scheduling was separated from the personal calendar.
The central website is in place.
The work calendar and issue form are embedded.
Navigation images and a reusable QR resource page were created.
QR access to the site and forms is established.
Supervisor permissions and notification ownership remain to be decided.

technical.summary: The document describes a web-based interface connecting calendar events, roster information, a Google issue form, visual navigation assets, and QR resources.
keyPoints: The page is intended for phone and computer access.
The work calendar was verified to contain events through Christmas.
Calendar event details and morning roster information are exposed through the site.
The Google issue form is embedded.
QR codes link users to the site and forms.
Editing permissions and notification delivery remain unverified.

projectSpecificLessons: The website can serve as the access layer for otherwise separate housekeeping tools.
Calendar cleanup should precede supervisor-facing calendar publication.
Roster visibility becomes more useful when attached to daily calendar events.
QR resources should be retained in a reusable location rather than treated as one-time outputs.
A functional interface still requires explicit access and notification governance.
generalLessons: Centralizing access can convert separate tools into a coherent operational system.
Visual navigation reduces the effort required to understand a multi-tool website.
Permission level and notification ownership are separate implementation decisions from interface construction.
A supervisor review meeting is most useful when framed around observable capabilities and unresolved decisions.
